title: Patch: an AI tuning screen counts the deals its change actually decided, and one that decided too few says it measured nothing instead of reading as a tie
thread:
**Issue #4319 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4319: Patch: an AI tuning screen counts the deals its change actually decided, and one that decided too few says it measured nothing instead of reading as a tie
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Before a new tuning value for the practice AI is kept, it gets a tryout. The changed AI plays 200 deals of cards against the unchanged one, each deal twice with the seats swapped, and the change is kept only if it clearly wins more. When the two AIs play a deal the same way, each wins one of its two games, so most deals end one-all whatever the change is worth. Today the report counts every such deal as evidence of a tie.

Once this is built, the report also says how many deals the change actually decided (won both games or lost both) and in how many it played differently at all. A tryout that decided too few deals to tell anything says so, instead of reading as 'no gain'.

An example: the setting that lets the AI picture its opponent going all in on a lethal attack was left off after a tryout that read 203 to 197. That tryout decided 3 deals of 200, and the change won all 3. No result on so few deals could have kept it. The maintainer and the bot, who tune the AI with these tryouts, are the ones who notice. Players get settings chosen on evidence rather than on noise.

## Why

`cargo jackioh arena --set improve-dev` (training/improve.md, A screen; R850000, R850001) decides whether each tuning value in `crates/ai/src/config.rs` is kept or dropped: keep it only when `edgeLow` > 0. The bot still screens this way: #4286 set `countdown_share` by screens (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:1034`). #4246, open and labelled needs decision, asks to screen `AI_REPLY.open_lethal` again, which SPEC §9.9 (`spec/09-architecture.md:167`) leaves off 'until a screen keeps it'.

A deal's edge is 1, 0 or -1 (`deal_edges`, `crates/tools/src/arena.rs:1184`). The interval is the mean plus or minus 1.96 standard errors over the deals (`paired_interval`, :1204). So a screen's recorded result and interval fix how many deals it decided. I put each screen recorded in config.rs back through that formula (a one-off Python check), and every one reproduces its recorded interval to three places:

| Knob (config.rs) | Recorded | Deals decided (won-lost) |
|---|---|---|
| `Windfury` 1.0 (#1602, :674) | 201-199, 0.005 (-0.005 to 0.015) | 1 (1-0) |
| `open_lethal` on (#1634, :1027) | 203-197, 0.015 (-0.002 to 0.032) | 3 (3-0) |
| `fatigue_draw` 1.0 (#1602, :769) | 199-201, -0.005 (-0.022 to 0.012) | 3 (1-2) |
| `countdown_share` 0.25 (#4286, :1034) | 200-200 (-0.014 to 0.014) | 2 (1-1) |
| `countdown_share` 0 (#4286, :1034) | 200-200 (-0.02 to 0.02) | 4 (2-2) |
| `enemy_face_down_per_cost` 0.8 (#1602, :764) | 201-199 (-0.017 to 0.027) | 5 (3-2) |
| `dormant_share` (#1506, :724) | 200-200 (-0.024 to 0.024) | 6 (3-3) |
| `dormant_share` 0.5 against 0 (:728) | 200-200 (0.0 to 0.0) | 0 |
| `graveyard_playable` 0.5 (#2928, :717) | 202-198 (-0.021 to 0.041) | 10 (6-4) |
| `defense_switches` (#1696, :1030) | 199-199 (-0.057 to 0.057) | about 34 (17-17) |

Nine of the ten decided 10 deals or fewer out of 200. Even a change that wins every deal it decides needs at least 4 decided deals before `edgeLow` can clear 0. So five of these screens could not have kept their change whatever happened. `open_lethal` is one of them: it was left off by a screen it won 3-0, and R4187000 describes a misplay that the off switch causes (the AI's model of the opponent walls and misses its own lethal).

The tight intervals come from the 190-odd deals that ended one-all. The two AIs probably played most of those identically: `r850000_one_ai_on_both_seats_splits_every_deal` (:1471) shows that an AI against itself plays a deal's two games to one hash. The report cannot tell 'the change never acted on these deals' from 'it acted and tied'. And improve.md step 4 forbids extending a screen, so an undecidable screen ends up read as a loss.

## Proposal

1. The paired tally (`Paired`, `tally`) adds:
   - `decided`: the deals whose edge is not 0, split into `wonBoth` and `lostBoth`;
   - `diverged`: the deals whose two games end on different hashes (`ArenaOutcome.hash`), meaning the two agents played differently at least once.
   The new keys go after `edgeHigh`, so code that reads the existing keys (`training/ml/retrain.sh`) keeps working.
2. A screen (`--set`) with fewer decided deals than a named `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` adds `inconclusive: true`. The proposed value is 20: at 20 decided deals the existing keep rule keeps a change that wins 15 of them, three in four. An inconclusive screen neither keeps nor drops a change. improve.md then says the knob is settled by its scene tests, and its config comment records the screen as inconclusive with its decided and diverged counts.
3. `--extend` on a screen keeps playing in batches of 100 deals until it has `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` decided deals or reaches a named cap, `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` (2,000, the promotion gate's own maximum). It reads the edge only at the end. The stop looks only at how many deals were decided, never at which way they went. Under a neutral change each decided deal is a fair coin however many there are, so this is not the 'extended because it came close' that step 4 forbids, and step 4 is amended to say so.
4. Each comment in config.rs that says a screen 'keeps nothing' adds the decided count its own recorded interval implies. No knob changes value in this patch.

A ruling note in the new issue's block records the counts and the inconclusive rule as extending R850000 and R850001, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<N>.md`.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`: `Paired`, `tally`, `Args` (`--extend`), the two constants and their tests.
- `training/improve.md` (A screen, steps 3 to 5), `training/README.md` (The arena and the agent), `crates/tools/README.md` (the arena row), `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` §14 (the tally's keys).
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs`: comments only.
- `spec/rulings/R<N>000.md`, `spec/pending/<N>.md`, and SPEC §9.9's training text if it states the keep rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The self-against-self paired test (`r850000_one_ai_on_both_seats_splits_every_deal`) tallies `diverged` 0 and `decided` 0.
- [ ] A unit test on hand-built outcomes holds `decided`, `wonBoth`, `lostBoth` and `diverged` to the edges and hashes given. A deal with a draw or an aborted game counts as decided when its edge is not 0.
- [ ] A screen with fewer than `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` decided deals prints `inconclusive: true` and one with that many or more does not. A paired series that is not on a seed set prints the counts and no verdict.
- [ ] `--extend` stops at the first batch where the decided count reaches the floor, or at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES`. A test shows the stopping point depends on the decided count alone: two outcome lists with the same decided deals but opposite signs stop at the same batch.
- [ ] The tally's JSON keeps every existing key in its existing order, with the new ones after `edgeHigh`. `retrain.sh`'s read of `edgeLow` is unchanged.
- [ ] improve.md, training/README.md, the tools README and SURFACE §14 describe the new keys and the inconclusive rule. The ruling note passes `cargo jackioh spec check`, with a proving test named after it.
- [ ] No value in `AI_EVAL`, `GREEDY_EVAL` or `AI_REPLY` changes.

## Size and risks

Medium: one tools module and its tests, four docs, comments in config.rs and a ruling note. Nothing changes in the engine, the AI's play or the client, and no game is played differently.

Risks:
- The existing tests that build a `Paired` literal or pin the tally's JSON tail change with the format. That extends them; it does not loosen any check.
- 20 is a judgment call: it is the point where the existing keep rule can keep a change that wins three deals in four. The ruling records the choice.
- `--extend` makes screening a rarely-acting change long. 2,000 games is roughly 2 to 4 hours at improve.md's 25 to 45 minutes per 400, which is why it is opt-in.

Out of scope: re-screening `open_lethal` or any other knob (#4246 and similar issues decide that with this report), and the promotion gate's report (`promote`, whose lanes are stopped or retired).

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44764407622)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`cargo jackioh arena` paired tallies count the deals a screen actually decided (`decided`, `wonBoth`, `lostBoth`) and the deals played differently (`diverged`), after `edgeHigh` so existing key order is kept. | File | New/change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/tools/src/arena.rs` | change | `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED`, `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES`, `SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS` constants; `Args.extend`; `Paired` fields; `decided_of`, `diverged_of`, `screen_done`; `tally()` `screen` param; `series()` extend check; `run()` extend loop; tests |

| `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` | change | §14.2: synopsis `[--extend]`, tally keys, inconclusive |
| `crates/ai/src/config.rs` | change | Comments only: decided (won–lost) counts on each screen comment; no value changes |

## Steps

1. In `crates/tools/src/arena.rs` beside `SCREEN_GAMES`, add with R4319000 doc comments: `pub(crate) const SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED: usize = 20;` (at 20 decided the keep rule keeps 15–5, three in four), `pub(crate) const SCREEN_MAX_GAMES: i32 = 2000;` (the promotion gate's maximum), `pub(crate) const SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS: i32 = 100;` (deals per `--extend` batch, 200 games).
2. Add `#[arg(long)] pub extend: bool` to `Args` with doc "R4319000: on a screen (`--set`), keep playing in batches of `SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS` deals until `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` deals are decided or `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` games are played".
3. In `series()`, first line: `if args.extend && args.set.is_none() { bail!("arena: --extend screens a seed set, so it needs --set improve-dev"); }`.
4. Extend `Paired` after `edge_high`, in this order: `pub decided: usize`, `pub won_both: usize`, `pub lost_both: usize`, `pub diverged: usize`, and `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub inconclusive: Option<bool>`. Field order is JSON order, so existing keys keep theirs. Rejected alternative: a plain `bool` (would print a key on passing screens and non-screens, against "does not [print inconclusive: true]").
5. Add helpers: `pub(crate) fn decided_of(edges: &[f64]) -> (usize, usize, usize)` counting `e != 0.0`, `e == 1.0`, `e == -1.0` (edges are exact halves); `pub(crate) fn diverged_of(outcomes: &[ArenaOutcome]) -> usize` counting `chunks(2)` with two games and differing `hash` (a trailing lone game never diverges); `pub(crate) fn screen_done(decided: usize, games: i32) -> bool` as `decided >= SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED || games >= SCREEN_MAX_GAMES`.
6. Change `tally` to `tally(a, b, outcomes, paired, screen: bool)`; in the `paired.then` block compute edges as today, then `let (decided, won_both, lost_both) = decided_of(&edges);`, `diverged_of(outcomes)`, and `let inconclusive = (screen && decided < SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED).then_some(true);`. Do not change `deal_edges` (promote.rs uses it).
7. In `run()`: `let screen = args.set.is_some();` play the initial `games` from `series()` with `deals_done = 0, games_done = 0`; per batch call `setups(&a, &b, batch_games, paired, |n| format!("{base}:{}", deals_done + deal_of(n)))`, renumber each game's `n` by `games_done`, `play_games`, accumulate outcomes, then `games_done += batch_games; deals_done += batch_games / 2;`. Batch size is `games` for the first batch, else `(SCREEN_MAX_GAMES - games_done).min(SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS * 2)` (both terms even, so deals stay whole). Break unless `args.extend && screen`, or when `screen_done(decided_of(&edges_of_all_outcomes), games_done)`. Streaming duel lines, records, and the single final `tally(..., paired, screen)` stay as today: the edge is read only at the end.
8. Update in-file tests: `screen()` helper gains `extend: false`; all `tally` calls gain the `screen` arg (`run`-equivalent: true in split test); Paired literal in `r850000_one_ai_on_both_seats_splits_every_deal` gains `decided: 0, won_both: 0, lost_both: 0, diverged: 0, inconclusive: None` plus asserts on `decided`/`diverged`; JSON tail in `r850000_the_paired_interval…` becomes `…"edgeHigh":1.0,"decided":0,"wonBoth":0,"lostBoth":0,"diverged":0}"`.
9. Add `#[cfg(test)] fn fake_outcome(result: Option<GameResult>, a_seat: PlayerId, hash: &str, n: i32) -> ArenaOutcome` (minimal `ArenaGame`: empty decks, `SelfAi`/`Random` seats, full skills, `labels` self/random, `paired: true`, `TEST_BUDGET`; other fields empty/zero) and three `r4319000_` tests (see Tests).
10. Docs: `training/improve.md` step 2 appends the new keys and `inconclusive: true` to the tally sentence; step 3 appends "A screen reading `inconclusive: true` neither keeps nor drops the change: the knob is settled by its scene tests, and its config comment records the screen as inconclusive with its decided count"; step 4 keeps the bans and appends "`--extend` is the one exception: decided in advance by the flag, it plays on in 100-deal batches to `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` decided deals or `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES`, reading the edge only at the end; the stop looks at how many deals were decided, never which way, so under a neutral change each decided deal is a fair coin however many there are"; step 5 records decided/diverged counts. Mirror the keys, inconclusive rule and `--extend` in `training/README.md` (arena section), the `crates/tools/README.md` arena row (add `[--extend]` to the synopsis), and SURFACE §14.2 (synopsis plus tally paragraph).
11. `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, comments only, append `; inconclusive (R4319000): N decided of 200 (won W, lost L)` to: `windfury` (1, 1–0), `open_lethal` (3, 3–0), `fatigue_draw` (3, 1–2), `countdown_share` 0.25 (2, 1–1) and 0 (4, 2–2), `enemy_face_down_per_cost` (5, 3–2), `dormant_share` first screen (6, 3–3) and 0.5-vs-0 screen (0), `graveyard_playable` (10, 6–4); `defense_switches` appends `; about 34 decided (17–17, R4319000)` without "inconclusive" (above the floor). Diverged counts are unrecoverable from recorded intervals and are not added.
12. Write `spec/rulings/R4319000.md` (front matter `id`, `title` answering what an undecidable screen means, `cards: "§9.9, R850000, R850001"`, `proven_in: [crates/tools/src/arena.rs]`; body: decided/wonBoth/lostBoth/diverged definitions incl. draws/aborts counting when edge ≠ 0; 20-deal floor with the 15-of-20 rationale; inconclusive neither keeps nor drops, knob settled by scene tests; `--extend` batches/stop/cap and why the count-only stop is not the forbidden close-read extension; Hearthstone has no counterpart) and `spec/pending/4319.md` with the `**[[R4319000]] … (issue #4319, 2026-11-20):** …` paragraph. Run `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Tests

- `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`, `r4319000_decided_won_lost_and_diverged_come_from_edges_and_hashes`: hand-built `fake_outcome`s — a both-won same-hash deal (decided, wonBoth, not diverged), a split different-hash deal (undecided, diverged), a draw-plus-a-win different-hash deal (decided, neither wonBoth nor lostBoth, diverged), an aborted-plus-a-loss deal (decided). Assert `tally` counts.
- `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`, `r4319000_a_short_screen_calls_itself_inconclusive`: decided < 20 with `screen=true` prints `"inconclusive":true`; 20 decided prints none; `screen=false` with decided < 20 prints none (build 20 won-both deals in a loop for the ≥20 case).
- `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`, `r4319000_extend_stops_on_the_decided_count_alone`: two batch-by-batch outcome lists with the same decided positions but opposite winners; assert `screen_done(decided_of(edges), games)` flips at the same batch for both.
- `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`, extend `series` tests: `--extend` without `--set` bails; with `--set` behaves as today.
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools arena`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Self-vs-self paired test tallies `diverged` 0 and `decided` 0.
- [ ] Hand-built test holds all four counts; draw/aborted deals count as decided iff edge ≠ 0.
- [ ] Below-floor screen prints `inconclusive: true`; at-floor and non-seed-set series do not.
- [ ] `--extend` stops at the first at-floor batch or `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES`; opposite-sign lists stop at the same batch.
- [ ] JSON keeps existing keys/order with new ones after `edgeHigh`; `retrain.sh` untouched, its `edgeLow` read unchanged.
- [ ] improve.md, training/README, tools README, SURFACE §14.2 updated; `cargo jackioh spec check` passes with an `r4319000` proving test.
- [ ] No value in `AI_EVAL`, `GREEDY_EVAL`, `AI_REPLY` changes; `cargo fmt --check` and clippy clean.

## Risks

- Existing `Paired` literal and JSON-tail tests break with the format; the plan extends them, loosening nothing.
- 20 is a judgment call (keep rule keeps 15-of-20); the ruling records it.
- `--extend` on rarely-acting changes runs long (≈2–4 h at 2,000 games); it is opt-in only.
- A trailing lone outcome (tests only; `series()` forces even paired counts) counts in edges as today and never as diverged.
- Config comments record decided (won–lost) only: diverged hashes are unrecoverable from recorded intervals.

## Open questions

None. Every choice is settled above; the builder asks a person only if R4319000 is taken and the next free R4319xxx block slot is unclear.
```

## Steps

1. In `crates/tools/src/arena.rs` beside `SCREEN_GAMES`, add with R4319000 doc comments: `pub(crate) const SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED: usize = 20;` (at 20 decided the keep rule keeps 15–5, three in four), `pub(crate) const SCREEN_MAX_GAMES: i32 = 2000;` (the promotion gate's maximum), `pub(crate) const SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS: i32 = 100;` (deals per `--extend` batch, 200 games).
2. Add `#[arg(long)] pub extend: bool` to `Args` with doc "R4319000: on a screen (`--set`), keep playing in batches of `SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS` deals until `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` deals are decided or `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` games are played".
3. In `series()`, first line: `if args.extend && args.set.is_none() { bail!("arena: --extend screens a seed set, so it needs --set improve-dev"); }`.
4. Extend `Paired` after `edge_high`, in this order: `pub decided: usize`, `pub won_both: usize`, `pub lost_both: usize`, `pub diverged: usize`, and `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub inconclusive: Option<bool>`. Field order is JSON order, so existing keys keep theirs. Rejected alternative: a plain `bool` (would print a key on passing screens and non-screens, against "does not [print inconclusive: true]").
5. Add helpers: `pub(crate) fn decided_of(edges: &[f64]) -> (usize, usize, usize)` counting `e != 0.0`, `e == 1.0`, `e == -1.0` (edges are exact halves); `pub(crate) fn diverged_of(outcomes: &[ArenaOutcome]) -> usize` counting `chunks(2)` with two games and differing `hash` (a trailing lone game never diverges); `pub(crate) fn screen_done(decided: usize, games: i32) -> bool` as `decided >= SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED || games >= SCREEN_MAX_GAMES`.
6. Change `tally` to `tally(a, b, outcomes, paired, screen: bool)`; in the `paired.then` block compute edges as today, then `let (decided, won_both, lost_both) = decided_of(&edges);`, `diverged_of(outcomes)`, and `let inconclusive = (screen && decided < SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED).then_some(true);`. Do not change `deal_edges` (promote.rs uses it).
7. In `run()`: `let screen = args.set.is_some();` play the initial `games` from `series()` with `deals_done = 0, games_done = 0`; per batch call `setups(&a, &b, batch_games, paired, |n| format!("{base}:{}", deals_done + deal_of(n)))`, renumber each game's `n` by `games_done`, `play_games`, accumulate outcomes, then `games_done += batch_games; deals_done += batch_games / 2;`. Batch size is `games` for the first batch, else `(SCREEN_MAX_GAMES - games_done).min(SCREEN_EXTEND_DEALS * 2)` (both terms even, so deals stay whole). Break unless `args.extend && screen`, or when `screen_done(decided_of(&edges_of_all_outcomes), games_done)`. Streaming duel lines, records, and the single final `tally(..., paired, screen)` stay as today: the edge is read only at the end.
